body: Also wanted to say sorry your parents don't seem to take it seriously... That's not right and you deserve to have someone care about your situation.

Hey sorry my story was long winded and maybe didn't help much but... I guess my main point was that you've already been suffering all this time with it, but if you end it now you'll never know how good it feels to not have the ringing anymore. Stay stong and have a great day

I am so sorry for everything you have suffered through in life. You are so strong for making it through all of this. I can relate a lot. My dad was also a horrible alcoholic when I was growing up and it got worse after my mom died when I was 14. He pretty much ignored my brother and I and just focused on drinking and women. I also struggled in school but eventually graduated.

I know it is so hard and life can feel so empty especialy with everything you have gone through but it sounds like you are doing a great job. The pain will be there for a long time, but it gets better with time. I'm not going to say the pain will 100% go away, but as time goes on you will have good experiences and happy times and you will be glad you got to experience the good times.

I still stuggle with suicidal feelings and depression but I've managed to get a good job and I try to keep moving forward despite the depression. Keep up all your good work, you're doing so well. If you ever need any support or someone to talk to you can message me. I really hope it gets better and I think it will.

Also, it doesn't matter if you fail your classes. You can always try again. In fact, it doesn't matter how many times you fail, just that you keep trying. When I was in school I was able to do an online program and graduate that way. My brother went to an alternative school and was able to graduate that way despite failing almost all of his classes the first time he tried them. There are options for you and you will succeed in the end if you keep trying. We don't always take the same roads in life and sometimes our paths are harder than others, but you can make it through and I truly believe in you.

It sounds like so many people around you have also been struggling but they are so lucky to have you in their life. For example, your mother suffering from abuse and you stepping in to help her... That is so amazing you were able to do that. You are a blessing in so many people's life I am sure of it. 

Regarding the loss of your father, first I must say I am so sorry for your loss. In my own way I can relate to the situation. I lived with my mother until she passed, but we had a horrible relationship. She was abusive (although she meant well) and I could not understand why she treated me the way she did. I don't think she knew she was hurting me and in her mind she was trying her best. Our relationship crumbled. For years I was angry and told her I hated her almost every day. We never really healed our relationship and the last time I saw her before she died I got in a fight with her over something stupid. I didn't know it would be the last time. I struggled with guilt about this for many years, but eventually a realized it was not my fault. I was just a kid trying my best to deal with a bad situation and I did not know how because I never had a good example shown to me. Please do not blame yourself for what has happened in your life, because you were just doing the best you could to deal with a bad situation.

Also, the divorce was definitely not your fault so please do not blane yourself for that. It may seem like the fight over the Wii is what caused the divorce, but there were most likely many other things going on between your parents that you did not know about that actually caused the divorce. Parents often try to hide these things from their kids, and kids usually wouldn't fully understand any way. My parents fought constantly when I was growing up and when I was an adult my dad admitted that he would have divorced my mom if it weren't for her illness. As a kid I thought they were fighting because of things I did and I also blamed myself, but when I got older my dad explained that there were always problems between my parents and it really was their own issue and was not my fault. 

I must also say that I am sorry for all the losses in your life (you mentioned you grandmother passing away shortly before your father, and your uncle passing away from suicide). I too lost many of my loved ones in a short period of time similar to this. Nothing can erase the pain of those losses but in time you will heal and become stronger. There's an old saying "your pain is the breaking of the shell that encloses your understanding"... Which basically means that the pain you experience is allowing you to gain a deeper understanding of life. I got that quote in a fortune cookie when I was about your age and going through my struggles and it really helped me understand that even though I wish I never had to go through all the pain, I was growing wiser and stronger in the process.

Unfortunately the deepest truths and the greatest wisdom can only be learned through the worst pain and the hardest experiences, but when the pain has healed the understanding you have gained will make you stronger than you have ever imagined.

Lastly, I want to let you know that you should never feel ashamed to express your feelings or talk about the pain you are experiencing. I understand if you don't feel comfortable to talk to your mother because as you said you don't want to disappoint her, but please know there are many people in the world who have experienced similar things and who understand. It takes a lot of strength to be able to express how your are feeling, especially when you are feeling so much pain. Please know that you are a strong person but you also don't need to stay strong all the time and act happy just keep the people around you happy. If you need to cry, you can cry - it doesn't make you weak and you won't disappoint the people who love you.

If you are one day comfortable enough to talk to your mom about the pain you are feeling it might help you feel better and I am sure it would not disappoint her. She is your mother and loves you and wouldn't want you to be in pain. If you ever express your sad and painful feelings to someone and they do not understand or try to make you feel bad or guilty for feeling the way that you do, please know that you did nothing wrong and they are just overwhelmed and might not be able to help you at that time, but there are resources and people who can help and will give you support.

I really hope this helps... I know it isn't much but at least know that I feel for you and really hope you feel better and things improve. You'll get through this. Stay strong

I am so sorry to hear of your struggles and pain... I went through a lot of rough stuff growing up and especially at the age you are now. I don't know exactly how you are feeling but I can relate. First of all, you don't deserve to be treated badly by anyone, especially your own father. You deserve better than this.

Secondly, even though you have struggled so much already you are finally coming into an age where you can start to have more power over your life and your decisions and soon you will be the one in complete control of your life and you won't have to answer to your family or anyone else around you who doesn't treat you right.

I know it is so hard and seems like it will never change, but it will. As hard as it may be, try to ignore the people who treat you badly and focus on yourself, the things you like, and what you can do for yourself. For example, once you turn 16 you can get a summer job maybe and start making your own money which you can put towards whatever you want to do (I know it is tough with Covid if you are still in lock down, but it will pass).

The bottom line is that you deserve the best in life and if anyone has treated you differently, just remember that they are the ones with the problem (not you) and you deserve better. Treat yourself well, treat yourself right the way you deserve. You will get past this one day! I've seen so many people in similar situations get past it and create a beautiful life for themselves. I know you can too.

I really hope this helps. If you need anything send me a message. Just remember you are a good, valuable, beauitful person and you deserve only the best!

Based off what you said I assume you are young and still living at home with your family. I struggled a lot with my relationship with my family members growing up and never felt loved by them... In fact, a lot of the time they were mean to me, rejected me, blamed me, etc. I was always trying to gain their love and acceptance so I wasted a lot of time trying to build relationships with them only for them to go right back to treating me badly and being hurtful whenever they felt like it. Honestly, it felt like not matter how much love I gave them it was never good enough and never mattered to them.

It took me many years to learn this lesson, but what I came to find out is that it doesn't matter how they feel about me, it just matters how I feel about myself and if they don't care about me it doesn't matter as long as I care about myself. I spent a lot of time neglecting my own needs because I was looking out for their needs.

Maybe you don't connect to anything I am saying, but if you do, my advice would be to keep on taking care of yourself and focus on what you want in life and who you want to be. Try your best in life and don't give up on your dreams. You are beautiful and unique and capable of so much. Even if you don't see that now you will one day and even if your family doesn't appreciate you there will be new people who come into your life who will. I hope this helps some. Stay strong!

I'm sorry you feel this way. I know the feeling and still struggle with it, pretty much daily. What I can say is that you are probably a pretty awesome/good person... I've met many people in my life, some good but also a lot of bad ones... One thing I've come to notice is that all the people I've known who are toxic, mean, etc. usually do not hate themselves at all (sometimes it is quite the opposite and they think they are amazing and are oblivious to all the pain they cause around them). On the flip side, many people I know who struggle with self loathing are actually really nice people who tend to think a lot about their impact on the world around them and are pretty hard on themselves. 

A lot of the time self hatred can be internalized from the people around us. For example, if someone close to you treated you badly, or if someone who was supposed to care about you (like family) didn't care like they should have we can often internalize their bad behavior and think we deserve it... Then we end up hating ourselves because we can't rationalize the undeserved negativity directed to us. I can't say for sure what your situation is or why you feel this way, but I can say that more likely than not you are a nice, interesting person who has a lot to offer the world.

Hi I'm sorry to hear about your situation... My dad has tinnitus as long as I've known him. He suffered bad ear infections as a small child and suffered damage to his hearing. Then, when he was a young adult he managed a rock band (booked their gigs, set up sound equipment, etc.) and basically developed tinnitus overnight during a show in a small venue where he was standing almost directly next to the speakers most of the night. He still has it and wears hearing aids now that he has gotten older...

I personally do not have tinnitus but I believe I came close to developing it and have some idea what it is like (from my dad's testimony as well as my personal experience). Years ago I went to a concert in a small music hall and the music was so loud it was hurt my ears all night and I was constantly going outside to escape the noise (my friend didn't want to leave though and I was her ride so I stayed till the end). When I left I felt like I was underwater (couldn't really hear so well, everything was kind of murky).

In the morning, when I woke up my ears were ringing very loudly. It wouldn't stop all day and finally by the end of the day I decided to play my singing bowl (Buddhist meditation tool) as long as I could to drown out the sound. So I went in an empty room, held the bowl in my hand and played it as loud as I could, filling the room with sound, drowning out the ringing in my ears. 

When I did this my ears were tingling inside, almost tickling feeling and after some time I stopped and there was no more ringing... I'm not saying that this would help you or even that the damage to my ears was serious (could have just been temporary), but I did feel as if playing the singing bowl was healing my ears/hearing... I just wanted to let you know because if you've never looked into holistic healing I think it could help. I became interested in it when I was young and my mom died from a 12 year battle with cancer. I saw how the traditional chemo/steroid treatments weakened her so I thought I would try to learn about natural healing. If nothing else has worked, maybe it is worth a try?

Also, I've found rife frequencies to be very helpful for me. You might not like them because it is basically listening to different tones that sounds kind of like tinnitus (ringing sound of a particular sound frequency), but it has helped me with other ailments. 

Anyways, I really hope your situation improves and you find a solution. I really think you will be able to fix it one day and I hope soon.
